Stair Calculator

Stair calculator: total rise to number of steps, riser height, total run and stringer length, checked against IRC limits.

Stair math

Divide total rise by the maximum riser height and round up to get the number of risers; then divide total rise by that number for the actual (equal) riser height. Treads = risers − 1 when the top floor acts as the last step. Total run = treads × tread depth, and the stringer is roughly √(rise² + run²).

Example: 108 in rise ÷ 7.75 = 13.9 → 14 risers of 7.71 in; 13 treads × 10 in = 130 in run; stringer ≈ √(108² + 130²) = 169 in.

Code limits (IRC residential)

  • Maximum riser height 7¾ in; minimum tread depth 10 in
  • Variation between risers or treads no more than 3/8 in
  • Minimum headroom 6 ft 8 in

Local codes may differ—check with your building department before cutting stringers. Add stringer length for the top connection and bottom cut.
